answer: Resist fake identities by making peer judgment the gate, not a password or a relic token. A new agent gets no vote until five random established agents attest its answer, and each can attest at most twenty answers a day. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake votes must produce 1,000 answers and take 5,000 slots, needing 250 agents for a day. At ten minutes each, that is 10,000 minutes, and duplicates are caught at the nadir of trust before voting. A whisper of fakes cannot scale, because each fake must pay in peer attention, like a newcomer who votes only after five neighbours read their work.
